steps.action: Sign and deliver articles of organization

source.quote: by signing and delivering articles of organization to the Commission for filing

steps.action: Check articles comply and fees paid

source.quote: No person shall conduct or transact business in the Commonwealth under any assumed or fictitious name unless such person files in the office of the clerk of the Commission a certificate of assumed or fictitious name.

gaps: The filing path models the LLC. Corporations (§§ 13.1-618, 13.1-818) and limited partnerships (§ 50-73.11) follow a similar delivery to the Commission, but their review and certificate sections are not printed here; a limited partnership is formed when its certificate is filed (§ 50-73.11(C)), and a partnership becomes a registered limited liability partnership when its statement of registration is filed (§ 50-73.132(A)).

§ 13.1-1011(D) says the Commission issues the certificate if the articles comply and the fees are paid; it does not say what happens when they do not (rejection, return or correction), so the 'not ok' branch ends without a stated result.

The review that applies § 13.1-1011(A) and (D) is implied; the printed text names the required contents but not who checks them or how long the check may take. No deadline for the Commission is stated.
The naming rules of § 13.1-1012 are not printed here; the 'name_ok' input stands for them.

LLC existence begins when the certificate of organization issues, or at a later time stated in the articles, but no later than 11:59 p.m. on the fifteenth day after issuance (§ 13.1-1004(B), (D)(1)). The single end event sits after the local licensing steps only because one BPMN end event cannot mark a midpoint; the LLC is formed at issue_certificate.

The assumed name branch is conditional: a company that does business under its exact registered name skips it, and the branches rejoin through an exclusive merge in front of the commissioner of the revenue's check.

§ 59.1-69(B) bars doing business under an assumed name before the certificate is filed; the schema has no 'before' deadline, so this stays in the step text. § 59.1-74(A) still speaks of 'the clerk of the court' keeping the book of certificates, while § 59.1-69(B) and § 59.1-74(B) send filings (since January 1, 2020) to the clerk of the Commission; who now keeps the register is not stated, so no recording step is modelled.

The local business license is applied for under each locality's own ordinance (§ 58.1-3703 only authorizes the fee and license taxes); the application step, who issues the license and the license tax rates are not in the printed text. The fee caps in § 58.1-3703(A) are $100, $50 and $30 by population, but localities over 50,000 had to reduce theirs to $50 by January 1, 2000, so the effective cap is $50 or $30. Many activities are exempt under § 58.1-3703(C).

§ 59.1-74(B) is phrased as a prohibition on the commissioner of the revenue; it applies only where the business uses an assumed or fictitious name. When no assumed name is used, the check passes trivially.

§§ 13.1-815.1 and 13.1-816 (nonstock corporation fees) are printed as effective until January 1, 2027; the versions that replace them are not printed here, so the nonstock fee in the comparison table may change on that date.

Virginia has both professional corporations (§ 13.1-544) and professional limited liability companies (§ 13.1-1103); the comparison table names the PLLC because it uses the LLC filing path and fee. The professional rule fires only when liability protection is wanted; a licensed professional without that need falls to the sole proprietorship or partnership rows.

The limited partnership rule fires before the LLC rule (the table's fixed priority) whenever protection and passive co-owners are both wanted, although the general partner stays liable (§ 50-73.24(A)); the output points owners who all need protection to the LLC.
The stock corporation charter fee depends on the number of authorized shares (§ 13.1-615.1(A)); the table states the formula and the amount for 25,000 shares or fewer.
State tax registration, employer registration, the annual registration fee and industry licences follow formation and are not modelled.
